$comment: Registry of recommended tools. The README is written from this file; scripts/check-registry.mjs and the weekly freshness workflow read it. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

tools.rationale: One binary for correctness (actionlint checks), security (zizmor audits) and policy (pinning, permissions, timeouts). Has --fix and --diff, SARIF, baselines.
tools.limitations: Created 2026-10-05, single maintainer, 7 releases. Parity with zizmor is self-reported. No pre-commit config audit, no LSP, no offline archived-uses.

tools.rationale: Linter and formatter in one fast binary; replaces Flake8, isort, pyupgrade and Black. Autofix, JSON/SARIF output, non-zero exit on findings.
tools.limitations: No type checking and no custom-rule plugin API. Pair with a type checker if you need one.

tools.rationale: Runs dozens of Go linters and the formatter in one pass with shared caching. v2 config, autofix, JSON/SARIF output. Custom analyzers can be built in with `golangci-lint custom`.
tools.limitations: Enable linters deliberately: the default set is small, and enabling everything produces noise. GPL-3.0 licensed binary.

tools.rationale: The official Rust linter, shipped with the toolchain. `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` fails CI on any finding.
tools.limitations: Versioned with the Rust toolchain through rustup, not through GitHub releases. Rust only.

tools.rationale: The standard Ruby linter and formatter, with autocorrect, JSON output and custom cops. Extensions cover Rails, RSpec and performance.
tools.limitations: Slower than Rust-based linters; use its server mode or cache locally. Extensions are separate gems.

tools.rationale: Finds bugs and portability problems in sh, bash, dash and ksh scripts. JSON and diff output, non-zero exit code.
tools.limitations: Stable-tool exception: the last release is v0.11.0 (2025-08-04), but the repository is still receiving commits. Does not support zsh. jactionlint already runs it on `run:` steps.

tools.rationale: Enforces Conventional Commits on a message, a range (`--from/--to`) or a hook. Needed if releases or changelogs are generated from commits.
tools.limitations: Requires Node. Checks format only, not whether the message is accurate.

tools.rationale: Config-file-driven Markdown linter with autofix and a maintained GitHub Action. Actively released through npm.
tools.limitations: Style and structure only; no prose or spelling checks. Versioned through npm tags rather than GitHub releases.

tools.rationale: Fast link checker for Markdown, HTML and plain text, with caching, retries and a GitHub Action.
tools.limitations: Network checks can be flaky: set a GitHub token so github.com links do not hit rate limits, and cache results.

tools.rationale: Source-code-aware spell checker built on a list of known misspellings, so false positives are rare and it needs little configuration. Fast, has autofix.
tools.limitations: Finds only known misspellings. For project dictionaries and many natural languages, cspell is the alternative; it is not recommended alongside typos.

tools.rationale: Finds unused files, exports and dependencies, with plugins for most frameworks and test runners. Non-zero exit on findings.
tools.limitations: Monorepos and unusual entry points need configuration. Never run with `--fix` unattended.

tools.rationale: Finds unused, missing and transitive dependencies in a Python project from its imports.
tools.limitations: Static import analysis: dynamic imports are missed. The repository moved to the osprey-oss organization; the latest release is 0.25.1 (2026-03-18).

tools.rationale: Project-specific syntax rules as YAML, with `ast-grep test` for rule fixtures and snapshots, so rules are themselves tested. Works for many languages with one tool.
tools.limitations: Syntactic matching only; no data-flow or taint analysis. Semgrep and its fork Opengrep cover that; see the under-review list.
